scope: Experimental sequential control and target SQL revocation on pinned PostgreSQL. Actual coordinator SIGKILL between commits, retry, target tombstones, absent/closed targets and OID replacement tested. Not an atomic cutoff, production integration or replay authorization.
checks: native local Linux daemon
host headroom checked before bounded probe
owned exact container is isolated and memory bounded
upstream bootstrap roles present
neighbor role is unprivileged without inherited memberships
native database OIDs are normalized before identity validation
coordinator killed after acknowledged control revocation
control token is durably revoked after crash
target remains active between the two revocation commits
control SQL cannot continue after first commit
target may still write before target revocation
retry acknowledges both phases with exact database identity
same database OID cannot substitute a different cluster
retry result binds exact original identity
completed target barrier denies old SQL
delayed target registration cannot resurrect old token
repeated complete revocation preserves evidence identity
only pre-barrier target data remains
target revoke initializes a durable tombstone before registration
absent target is recorded only after control revoke
late guarded creation cannot materialize absent target
absent target stays absent
closed target does not become completed barrier evidence
closed target remains closed
closed target failure still retains control revocation
target replacement prevents reuse of old database evidence
disposable database did not OOM
exact disposable container absent from successful inventory
